text: NeoXider MCP Hub 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 MCP 能力代理，将多个 MCP 服务器和本地技能收进同一目录，并只向模型提供一个常驻工具。模型可搜索和检查能力，按需启动服务器、筛选或调用其工具，再停止服务器；技能则按需读取。它还支持配置、状态查询、提案与分页，适合希望减少常驻工具描述、统一管理多个 MCP 能力的用户。运行需要 Node.js 22.19 或更高版本。

NeoXider MCP Hub is a DeepSeek Harness broker for MCP servers and local skills. One tool searches the catalog, inspects and starts servers on demand, lists and calls their tools, stops servers, and loads skills when needed. It also supports proposals and paging. Requires Node.js 22.19+.

NeoXider MCP Hub 的功能「目录搜索」：按关键词或能力类型查找目录中的 MCP 服务器和技能，并返回匹配条目。 通过 capability_hub 的对应 action 触发。
NeoXider MCP Hub 的功能「按需发现和调用工具」：按需启动 MCP 服务器，列出或筛选它的工具，并将参数转发给选中的工具。 通过 capability_hub 的对应 action 触发。
NeoXider MCP Hub 的功能「本地技能加载」：从已批准目录读取单个本地技能文件，并把技能正文返回给客户端。 通过 capability_hub 的对应 action 触发。
NeoXider MCP Hub 的功能「能力提案」：将新的服务器或技能保存为待审提案，供人审核后再批准。 通过 capability_hub 的对应 action 触发。

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Introduction：Every MCP server you configure puts all of its tool schemas into every prompt, whether or not the task touches a tool. Ten servers can cost roughly 15,000 tokens before the model has read your question, and a crowded tool list makes the model pick worse.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Introduction：NeoXider MCP Hub is a stdio MCP server that exposes **one** tool, `capability_hub`. The model searches a lightweight catalog, inspects permissions, wakes the one server it needs, calls it, and shuts it down again. Skills live in the same catalog and are loaded one at a time, only when selected.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Introduction：| | |
|---|---|
| **One resident tool** | The host carries about 420 tokens, however many servers you configure. |
| **MCP servers and skills together** | One catalog, one `search`, one trust model. Servers start on demand; skill bodies load one at a time. |
| **Stopped, not just hidden** | A capability is a process that is off until the model asks for it. `disable` stops it. |
| **Human approval** | A model can *propose* a server or a skill. Only a person, outside the model, can approve it. |
| **Any MCP client** | A plain stdio server: OpenCode, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, DeepSeek Harness. |
| **Measured, including the losses** | Context, accuracy, a head-to-head and a dynamic proof are reproducible scripts in [`bench/`](bench) — the one where Tool Search wins is published too. |

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · How it works：- One fixed schema stays in the prompt. Child tool schemas stay outside the model's context until requested.
- `tools` returns names and descriptions by default; full schemas are opt-in. It starts the server itself, so `enable` is optional.
- MCP processes start lazily and live only as long as the hub process.
- Skills are discovered by metadata and loaded one at a time.
- Third-party additions enter a human approval queue; the model cannot approve executable code.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Quick start：Requirements: Node.js 22.19+ and pnpm.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/NeoXider/neoxider-mcp-hub.git
cd neoxider-mcp-hub
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test

The default catalog contains only a bundled echo MCP and an example ML skill. Tests do not download or execute third-party packages.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Quick start：The client takes simple requests as plain flags (`--action`, `--query`, `--kind`, `--name`, `--tool`). A request with arguments goes in a file, `pnpm client -- --input request.json`, because Windows PowerShell 5.1 strips the double quotes from inline JSON passed with `--json`.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Connect your client：The hub is a plain stdio server. Launch it from npm, with nothing to clone or build:

```bash
npx -y @neoxider/mcp-hub --catalog /abs/path/catalog.json --state /abs/path/state
```

Keep your own catalog and state in folders that last. The package's bundled `data/` holds only the demo entries, and under `npx` it sits in a cache that can be cleared, taking your approvals with it. A new catalog can start empty:

```json
{ "version": 1, "entries": [] }
```

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Connect your client：From a checkout instead (after `pnpm build`), replace `npx -y @neoxider/mcp-hub` with `node /abs/path/neoxider-mcp-hub/dist/src/server.js`; without `--catalog` and `--state` it then uses the checkout's own `data/` folder. Use absolute paths either way.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Claude Code：```bash
claude mcp add capability_hub -- npx -y @neoxider/mcp-hub --catalog /abs/path/catalog.json --state /abs/path/state
```

Every example names the server `capability_hub`, with an underscore. Clients that prefix MCP tools with the server name then show one spelling everywhere, and a model that has seen the tool under one client does not reach for `capability-hub` under another.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · DeepSeek Harness：Install the published bundle — no paths to edit, no build on your machine:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/NeoXider/neoxider-mcp-hub/releases/download/v0.10.3/neoxider-mcp-hub-0.10.3.tgz
```

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · DeepSeek Harness：Restart Harness. The hub runs inside the host process as one native model-facing tool, `capability_hub`. The catalog and state default to the installed package's `data/` directory; to keep them elsewhere, set the row's `catalogPath` / `stateDir` Config in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. `toolCallTimeoutMs` raises the per-call ceiling from its 300,000 ms default, and `pageChars` sets the page size.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · DeepSeek Harness：A built checkout loads the same way without packing it: insert the compiled entry by path. The plugin imports nothing from Harness at runtime, so it works from outside the profile's `node_modules`.

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: capability-hub
      name: /abs/path/neoxider-mcp-hub/dist/src/dsh-plugin.js
      config:

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · DeepSeek Harness：Prefer the native tool with a local model. The alternative is a stdio child through the in-box MCP client: build the hub, then merge [`examples/dsh/cordis.patch.yml`](examples/dsh/cordis.patch.yml) into the active Harness Web profile and adjust the absolute repository path. Harness then exposes the tool as `mcp__capability_hub__capability_hub`, a long name that repeats itself. Small models sometimes misspell it, for example as `mcp__capability-hub__…`, and a server that only recognizes declared tool names then returns the whole call as plain text, so it never runs.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · DeepSeek Harness：The native plugin also recovers such calls. When a model reply has no tool call and its text ends in a written call to the hub under any of these spellings (`<tool_call>` in Qwen's XML or JSON form), the plugin turns it into a real `capability_hub` call. Older chats that remember the MCP name therefore keep working, and no alias tool is added to the prompt. Quoted examples, cut-off calls and calls to other tools are left as text.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Share one catalog between clients：Every client starts **its own** hub process, but the catalog and the approvals are plain files. Give each client the same flags and they see the same capabilities and the same approvals:

```text
node dist/src/server.js --catalog /abs/path/catalog.json --state /abs/path/state
```

Approve a server once, and every client that uses that `--state` can start it. Give a client its own `--state` when you want its approvals kept apart.

text:
@neoxider/mcp-hub README · One catalog for MCP servers and skills：- MCP transports: `stdio` and `streamable-http`.
- Templates: `${catalogDir}`, `${packageDir}` and explicitly allowlisted `${config:key}` values.
- Secrets: environment-variable references only. Secret-like model configuration keys are rejected.
- Skills: approved local Markdown files, limited to 256 KiB. Resolved paths must remain under the catalog or package directory; an external directory needs an explicitly reviewed `skill.allowedRoots` entry.
- State: runtime config and proposals are ignored by Git.
section: One catalog for MCP servers and skills

text:
@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Human-gated installation：


The model proposes. A person approves, outside the model.

Model-created proposals are stored under `data/state/pending` and cannot execute. Approve from a separate, human-operated command:

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Human-gated installation：Without `--catalog` and `--state`, `admin` uses the same defaults as the server (the package's `data/` folder), so an approval typed from any directory lands where the server reads it. Then call `catalog.reload` and `enable`. Prefer pinned package versions or immutable Git revisions; avoid floating `latest` installers in approved entries. Removing an entry or clearing its `trusted` flag and calling `catalog.reload` also stops a server that is already running.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Human-gated installation：Ready-to-review proposals are included for [Web Search Neo](examples/catalog/web-search-neo.proposal.json) (dynamic web research and browser tooling) and [Unity CLI MCP](examples/catalog/unity-cli.proposal.json) (the official Unity CLI transport; its tool list is populated only while a Unity Editor with Unity Pipeline is connected). They are examples, not silently trusted defaults: review paths, versions and permissions before approval.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Model-facing contract：The public schema is intentionally flat so constrained-decoding engines such as LM Studio can compile it reliably. It uses only the keywords every client accepts: `type`, `properties`, `required`, `enum`, a boolean `additionalProperties` and descriptions. Length limits are checked on input rather than advertised as `maxLength`. Call arguments travel as a structured `arguments` object; the remaining payloads (configuration, proposals) travel as JSON strings.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Model-facing contract：| Action | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `search` | Search compact capability metadata; `kind` filters to `mcp` or `skill` |
| `inspect` | Review one capability, its permissions, configuration and environment status |
| `configure` | Set allowlisted non-secret values through `payloadJson` |
| `enable` / `disable` | Start or stop one trusted MCP |
| `tools` | List child tools; `query` narrows the list, schemas remain optional |
| `call` | Proxy one child tool call through the `arguments` object (`payloadJson` also works, but the two must not be combined) |
| `skill.load` | Load one approved local skill body |
| `propose` | Store an untrusted proposal from `payloadJson` |
| `proposals` | List pending proposals |
| `catalog.reload` | Reload approved catalog state |
| `page` | Read the next page of a long call result, with the `cursor` printed on its last line |
| `status` | List running capabilities |

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Measured results：Everything below is produced by scripts in [`bench/`](bench), and the raw outputs are committed, so every table can be re-derived without network access: per-tool measurements under [`bench/snapshots/`](bench/snapshots), the token report in [`bench/results.json`](bench/results.json), the accuracy report in [`bench/accuracy.json`](bench/accuracy.json), the comparison in [`bench/head-to-head.json`](bench/head-to-head.json) and the lifecycle receipt in [`bench/dynamic-proof.json`](bench/dynamic-proof.json). The full write-up, failure analysis and prior art are in [docs/context-economy.md](docs/context-economy.md).

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Context savings：[`bench/measure.mjs`](bench/measure.mjs) starts each **real, published** MCP server over stdio, asks for `tools/list`, and counts the tokens (`o200k_base`) of the exact JSON a host injects per tool (`name` + `description` + `inputSchema`). The hub is measured the same way, by starting it and reading its own `tools/list`.

```powershell
pnpm bench
```

|---|---|---:|---:|

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Context savings：The hub publishes one schema no matter how many servers you configure, so the classic side grows linearly while the hub side grows only by a line of catalog prose per entry — and stops growing once the list degrades to names only. Each hub figure below is measured by starting the real server against a catalog of that size, not projected:

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Context savings：| Servers configured | Classic tokens | Hub resident | Saved |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 6,200 | 430 | 93.1% |
| 10 | 15,500 | 584 | 96.2% |
| 20 | 31,000 | 826 | 97.3% |
| 30 | 46,500 | 468 | 99.0% |
| 60 | 93,000 | 595 | **99.4%** |

The drop at 30 is the degradation firing: full descriptions no longer fit the budget, the list falls back to names, and the resident cost roughly halves.

</details>

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Context savings：| Scenario | Path | Hub tokens | vs 6,200 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| **idle** — task needs no capability | resident schema only | 422 | **93.2%** saved |
| **direct** — task opens one capability | `search` + `tools` with a query | 554 | **91.1%** saved |
| **cautious** — also reviews permissions, reads the full list | `search` + `inspect` + `enable` + `tools` | 1,195 | 80.7% saved |

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Context savings：The direct row still charges a `search`, which the inlined catalog list often makes unnecessary — a conservative choice, since the bias should run against our own number.

The direct path is cheap for two reasons that were already in the code while the benchmark was ignoring them: **`tools` starts the server itself**, so `enable` is not on the critical path, and **`tools` accepts a query**, costing 60 tokens instead of 558 when the agent already knows what it wants:
@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Context savings：</details>

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Tool-selection accuracy：Saving context is worthless if the model then picks the wrong tool. So that is measured too, against **Qwen3.8-27B** running locally at temperature 0 — 28 tasks with known answers, of which **6 need no tool at all** and calling one is scored as a failure.

```powershell
pnpm bench:accuracy
```

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Tool-selection accuracy：| Condition | Resident | Overall | No-tool tasks | False calls | Avg turns | Avg prompt |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **classic** — 47 schemas resident | 6,200 | **96.4%** | 83.3% | **1** | 1 | 7,269 |
| hub, vague catalog | 422 | 82.1% | 83.3% | 1 | 3.00 | 2,818 |
| hub, list not inlined | 328 | 85.7% | 100% | 0 | 3.54 | 3,047 |
| **hub, as shipped** | 533 | **96.4%** | 100% | **0** | 1.96 | **1,873** |

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Tool-selection accuracy：**Same accuracy on a twelfth of the resident context — and fewer total tokens.** 1,873 prompt tokens per task against 7,269, summed across every turn of the multi-turn protocol. The penalty a broker is supposed to pay for extra round trips did not appear.

The classic setup's single failure is worth naming: asked *"Is 97 a prime number?"*, the model with 47 tools resident reached for `sequentialthinking`. Every hub condition with a usable catalog scored 100% on the no-tool tasks.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Tool-selection accuracy：The vague-catalog row is the same code and the same servers — only the descriptions differ. **Write your catalog so it can be found**; it is worth ~14 points.

The hub rows are multi-turn against live child processes, so borderline tasks move a few points between runs. Across three runs the classic condition reproduced at exactly 96.4% every time and the shipped hub scored 96.4–100%; the two ablation rows always landed below both, never above.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Head to head against Tool Search：Everything above compares this broker to a static configuration, which cannot support a claim of being better than the *other* lazy approaches. So they were measured too — same 28 tasks, same model, and a `tool_search` condition built the way Anthropic's Tool Search Tool and Claude Code's MCP Tool Search work, with real semantic retrieval.

```powershell
pnpm bench:head-to-head
```

text:
@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Head to head against Tool Search：**Read this honestly: it is a tie on accuracy, and Tool Search is the more compact design.** 75 resident tokens against 709, and it does not grow with the catalog, because its resident surface is one query string. This project's surface carries an action enum, a payload field and an inlined capability list.

What both lazy approaches do beat is a static list: about a fifth of the prompt tokens, and 100% on the six tasks where the correct answer is to call nothing, against classic's 83.3%.

text: @neoxider/mcp-hub README · Head to head against Tool Search：Where this broker still earns its place is the axis none of these numbers cover — it keeps capabilities **stopped**, not merely hidden, and it carries permissions, configuration and human approval that a search tool has no opinion about. The comparison is also unfair in our favour in one way that is spelled out in the write-up: the Tool Search index assumes every server has already been enumerated, and its embedding model is not charged for.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Prompt-cache friendly by design：


One hub, any client, one shared catalog.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Prompt-cache friendly by design：Local servers such as Strata and llama.cpp reuse the longest unchanged *start* of the prompt, so anything that rewrites an earlier part of the conversation makes them read the whole rest again. The hub keeps its part of the prompt stable:

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Prompt-cache friendly by design：Measured on Strata 0.2.3 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M, 128K, one slot) through DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2 and this hub driving web-search-neo, with a long page that came back in two pages: every request after the first of a session reused the cached start and read only what was new — 7,701 of 7,774, 10,367 of 12,246, 16,442 of 18,328 tokens — and the next turn of the same session, a new process resuming it, reused 20,006 of 20,067.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Troubleshooting：**A skill or a long result arrives as a bare `{"name": …}` or `{"paged": true, …}`.** Some MCP clients, OpenCode among them, show a tool's `structuredContent` and ignore its text. From 0.10.0 the body travels in both: `instructions` for `skill.load`, `text` for paged results. On an older build, update the hub and restart the client's hub process.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Troubleshooting：**The hub exits at start with `--page-chars` / `CAPABILITY_HUB_PAGE_CHARS` must be a non-negative integer.** The value was not a number. `0` turns paging off; an empty value is ignored.

@neoxider/mcp-hub README · Current scope：- Tool calls are proxied; child MCP resources and prompts are not bridged yet.
- Reconnect is explicit: `disable`, then `enable`.
- Remote skill download, signature verification and sandboxed installers are future work.
- Distribution is the npm package `@neoxider/mcp-hub`, a Git checkout, or the Harness bundle from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NeoXider/neoxider-mcp-hub/releases).
- A model with unrestricted host shell access can bypass plugin-local policy; use Harness permissions as the outer boundary.
